1.sofaString: 112	Pt, ***** ********, is a 14-month-old female with diagnosed cardiomyopathy, referred by ***** ******, ****, Transplant Coordinator, for Psychosocial Assessment for Heart Transplant Evaluation.  Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the patient's mother, ***** ********, and review of the medical records. *****'s father, ******* ********, was not available due to caring for their older child at home.  SW spent approximately 40 minutes of face-to-face time with patient and family.     Living situation:  **, *****, lives with her mother, father, and brother in *********, *******. They reside at **** ****** ****, *********, ** *****. They are currently renting a 3-bedroom ******** with central heating and a/c.  They are building a 5-bedroom **** ** ***** ********** *****, ****** ******, ** *****, that is expected to be completed on ******* ***. There is no smoking in the home.       Demographics:  Mother:  ***** ********  DOB:  **/**/****  Language: English  Education Level: BSN and ******'s ****** in ********** *********  Employment:  Stay at **** ***  Phone:  ***-***-****     Father:  ******* ********  DOB:  **/**/****  Language: English  Education Level: ******'s ******  Employment:  Software ******** with ********  Phone:  ***-***-****     Siblings:  ***** ********- 11 (received heart transplant **/**/**)     Social History and Support Systems:  ***** resides at home in Kissimmee with her mother, father, and brother. ***** and ******* have been married for 17 years. They lean on each other for support and work their schedules around the children. The maternal grandparents have also relocated to *******. They are currently living an hour away from family in *********** but may eventually relocate closer to the family.   Patient's brother, *****, received a heart transplant on **/**/** at ****** ********'s Hospital and is still followed by their transplant team. Mom reports that he has a stable course post-transplant. They are working with him now on medical independence and teaching him to fill his pillbox.   ***** and ******* struggled with fertility while trying to get pregnant with the children. They had several miscarriages and also lost a child born prematurely at 23 weeks. Mom reports they coped appropriately with the losses and do not plan on having any further children.  Mom reports that ***** is on track developmentally. There have never been any developmental concerns by parents or pediatrician. Mom reports that ***** defers from her brother in her personality. While at a younger age he was laid back, ***** is determined, strong-willed, and very independent. Mom is hopeful that they will be able to await transplant outpatient as this will be easier on ***** and the family.    Mom will be *****'s primary caregiver post transplant. Dad will be the backup caregiver. He is the sole provider for the family but can work from anywhere and can adjust his work times as needed. Maternal grandparents have also helped greatly in the past.   Mom denies any objections to blood products, transfusions, etc.     Course of illness:     ***** was diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy at 18 days of age on screening echo done because of her family history: her brother had a heart transplant for dilated cardiomyopathy. She has been asymptomatic since then with good feeding tolerance, appropriate growth, no cyanosis or edema and no other sign of heart failure. Mom reports that *****'s heart function has been slowly declining since diagnosis.      Financial situation:  ******* works full time and is the sole provider for the family. His income more than meets their needs each month. Due to family income, they will not be eligible for SSI or ***** assistance. Family has experienced the costs of transplant in the past and deny any need for fundraising information.  ***** is covered by United Healthcare through *******'s employer. Dad will likely only need limited time off work since mom is not working, his schedule is flexible, and grandparents are retired.             Both parents have vehicles and transportation will not be a barrier.      Family History:  Mom denies any DCF, law enforcement, or substance abuse history by immediate family.      Dad has a history of depression, per mom, likely stemming from the loss of his mother at a young age. He has engaged in counseling sporadically but is not currently involved. Mom reports that he is on Effexor and the depression does not interfere with his daily functioning.      Adherence:  There are no concerns with adherence noted. Family is familiar with transplant regimen and there is no documented compliance issues.      Assessment and recommendations:  Family is very knowledgeable about transplant as their 11 year old son received a heart transplant in **** ** ****. There were no concerns noted during assessment or in medical records. Family is ready to proceed with transplant if indicated.
